title: Guacamole
subtitle: fresh avocado dip with lime and chilli
excerpt: Creamy mashed avocado mixed with lime, chilli, tomato, and fresh coriander. It takes 10 minutes and no cooking. Eat it fresh -- avocado discolours if left too long.
sourceNotes: Guacamole originates with the Aztecs of central Mexico, who made a sauce called ahuacamolli from avocado and tomato. The dish has been made in Mexico for thousands of years.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make no more than 1 hour ahead. Press cling film directly onto the surface to slow discolouration.

content.text: Use ripe avocados -- press the tip gently and it should give a little. Mash with a fork, not a blender. A rough texture is better than a smooth puree.

items.prepNote: use 3 ripe avocados, halved and stoned -- mash the flesh
or 1 small fresh chilli, finely chopped
use a handful of fresh coriander leaves, finely chopped

content.text: Halve the avocados and remove the stones. Scoop the flesh into a bowl.
Add the lime juice and salt. Mash roughly with a fork, leaving some texture.
Stir in the diced onion, tomato, chilli, and coriander.
Taste and adjust the lime juice, salt, and chilli. Serve immediately.

items.fix: Press cling film directly against the surface with no air gaps. The lime juice also slows browning -- use plenty.
Guacamole needs generous salt and acid. Add more lime juice and salt a little at a time, tasting after each addition.
Mash with a fork and stop when it is a rough, chunky paste. Some avocado texture makes a better dip.

content.text: Guacamole has been made in Mexico for thousands of years. The Aztecs made a version called ahuacamolli, meaning avocado sauce, long before European contact. The avocado is native to Mexico and Central America. Today guacamole is one of the most widely eaten dips in the world, especially popular across North America.
